svg.title: viber - from an idea to committed code
svg.desc: Flow diagram of the viber plugin: one-time setup, the optional UI prototype and the two entries, an idea through the intent interview and a bug through the fixer diagnosis. The interview ends in one of three paths. The full path writes a spec with the spec-writer and spec-reviewer agents, then a plan with two plan-mapper agents, the plan-writer and the plan-reviewer, and stops at the gate where you approve the plan. The short path writes a short plan, stops at its own gate and builds through simple-implementor, which is also where a direct bug fix lands. The direct path builds in the same session through implementor. The short and the direct path leave the change uncommitted. After the full path's gate, spec-implementor relays between a script and the agents: task-coder, task-reviewer and one commit per task, tasks in parallel where they share no file, a task past its fix rounds held while the rest goes on. The build closes with the final review, the full test run, the memory, rules and QA writers together, the project's own extension agents, the finalizer and the archive of the run, followed later by the e2e pass that turns the QA scenarios into Playwright tests.

From an idea to committed code
skill - runs in your own session
agent - its own fresh context
gate - waits for your decision
optional
your call, or its switch is on
build.qa
a switch in .claude/viber.yml
skill
/setup
once per project - seeds .claude/viber.yml (the switches below) and the .gitignore rules, merges the recommended permissions
into .claude/settings.json, checks the gh CLI and that CLAUDE.md names your build and test commands
New idea · feature · change to something existing
Bug · regression · wrong behaviour
a UI change
otherwise
optional
skill
/ui-prototype
An HTML mockup of the UI change in your project's own look,
one proposal or three variants, settled in conversation.
its Mockup: line
skill
/intent
Asks in rounds of at most 5 questions, each with options and a recommendation.
Looks the facts up in your code itself; the decisions stay yours.
Ends in a shared understanding that you confirm.
with it you pick the path: the full one, a short plan, or a build right away
a UI change with no mockup yet: it offers /ui-prototype first
skill
/fixer
Traces the bug to its root cause in the code.
Proves it with one failing test, left red in your tree.
Never fixes it itself.
then you pick: a short plan first, or the fix right away
Spec → Plan → Build
Build now
Short plan → Build
Plan → Build
Fix directly → Build
skill
spec
Writes down every fact the interview settled, one numbered line each.
The spec-writer agent turns them into the spec; a script checks its sections.
The spec-reviewer agent reviews it once against those facts; a FAIL is fixed.
a gap the interview left comes back to you as a question
docs/_specs/<stamp>_<slug>/spec.md
you confirm the spec
skill
planner
Two plan-mapper agents index where the spec lands: in the code, in the tests.
The plan-writer agent writes the tasks; a script checks and lands the plan,
then derives each task's wave and model.
a spec with a decision: the adr agent stages its record for docs/adr/
one plan · numbered tasks · DoD and Verify per task
agent
plan-reviewer
Reviews the landed plan against the spec, before you see it.
critical problems only · a second FAIL comes back to you
FAIL → fix
PASS
GATE - you approve the plan
a hook refuses to leave plan mode without a PASS on the landed plan
skill
implementor
Builds in this session, stage by stage,
one simple-coder agent per stage.
Then one full test run, with repairs.
no plan, no review: picking this path approves the edits
skill
simple-plan
Writes what was settled as a short plan,
one fact per line, for a fresh context.
GATE - you approve the plan
accepting it clears the context
skill
simple-implementor
Splits the plan into stages, one simple-coder agent
per stage, then one full test run.
A code review follows, its findings fixed once.
stages that share no file run side by side
a direct bug fix lands here with no plan and no gate
the change stays uncommitted in your work tree
you look at it first · /commit commits it when you say so
accepted: the context is cleared, the plan stands alone
BUILD - the approved plan, task by task
skill
spec-implementor
Only relays: a script decides every step, the skill sends the agents it names.
A task starts once every task it runs after is done.
up to 5 agents at once · tasks that share a file run in turn
the run's state is committed as it goes: an interrupted build resumes, on any machine
docs/_specs/<stamp>_<slug>/
FOR EVERY TASK (SOME IN PARALLEL)
agent
task-coder
Builds one task and proves it with the task's own check.
gets only its task file · on the model the plan set: haiku, sonnet or opus
a failed check sends it once more, a second one holds the task
skipped for a task with no runtime code
agent
task-reviewer
Gates the task against its task file and its diff.
runs the check itself and ties every DoD clause to the code
a Critical finding opens a fix round, at most 2 a task
FAIL → fix
commit - one task, one commit
T<n> - <title> · only that task's files · your hooks run
next ready task
past 2 fix rounds
held
The task stops, its findings go to
the outcome. Tasks running after it
are skipped, the rest of the plan goes on.
the run stays open, with no archive:
build the plan again to retry
when no task is left to start
agent
final-reviewer
Reviews the whole build for what no single task shows:
a requirement nothing delivers, a consumer left broken.
Critical findings are fixed once, in a commit of their own
agent
final-tester
Runs your build and the full test suite, without end-to-end tests.
a failure goes to a repair coder, at most 2 rounds
the three writers run together
agent
memory-writer
Your CLAUDE.md files learn what the build taught.
the nodes below the root · the root one gets suggestions
at most 600 bytes of net growth a build
agent
rules-writer
Corrects the rules the build made false.
only in .claude/rules/viber/, at most 200 bytes of growth
build.rules false: skipped
optional
agent
qa-writer
Test scenarios for what was actually delivered:
qa.md for a person, qa.e2e.md as the handoff for /e2e
build.qa true · posted to the plan's issue as a comment
optional
agent
your extensions
Your own agents from .claude/agents/, run in the listed order.
one commit per agent · /extension writes one and registers it
build.extensions not empty
agent
finalizer
Writes the summary on top of the run's outcome:
delivered, not delivered, spec drift, what is next for you
archive - the finished run, in one commit
keeps the spec, the outcome, the mockup and the QA documents
docs/_specs/<stamp>_<slug>/ → docs/specs/
later, when you want them automated
skill
/e2e
Turns the QA scenarios into Playwright tests,
one scenario at a time.
a test counts only once it runs green · left uncommitted
